nodes.statement: In pure zero-field SK with xi(t)=t^2/2, for every gamma in U (nonnegative, nondecreasing, right-continuous and L1 on [0,1)), the control value Phi with terminal |x| is even, convex, one-Lipschitz, and |x|<=Phi(t,x)<=|x|+sqrt(2(1-t)/pi)+(1/2)int_t^1 gamma. Every positive spatial derivative is bounded and jointly continuous on [0,T]xR for T<1, locally absolutely continuous in time and satisfies the differentiated PDE almost everywhere. Jointly strongly commuting controls may be substituted when joint exponentials and coefficient/adjoint jets have polynomial weighted bounds; Fourier tails are controlled before removing the cutoff.
nodes.boundary: Uniformity concerns a fixed finite calculation, bounded parameter sets and specified weighted norms. It does not imply global operator-norm convergence, a nondegenerate covariance assumption, or uniformity in growing word length.

nodes.label: Ordinary cost and mixer root updates
nodes.statement: For a fixed finite ordinary cost/mixer word, the embedded root maps and adjoints have smooth weighted limits. A mixer updates u to exp(−iβX)u; a cost updates u to exp(−it Z q(v_Z))u, where v_Z=u*ZuΩ is the preceding child insertion. The cost leaves that insertion unchanged. The fixed-word tree value is E(v_Z).

nodes.label: Smooth exclusion-gate calculus
nodes.statement: For a fixed finite exclusion-gate expression, every transmitted column is centered by parity; receiver, path-ancestor and control-target masks are disjoint as prescribed; controls lie in one commuting algebra and a target may contribute its seed but not its spin. Root maps, adjoints and insertions converge in the weighted topology and obey occupation estimates. Finite local replacements with common parameter expressions, convergent jets and adjoint jets, and uniform polynomial bounds converge inside each fixed surrounding word. A root-mask column has weighted norm at most C√p.
nodes.boundary: Measurable seed masks are permitted through bounded subsequences with Gaussian almost-everywhere convergence. Grouped finite control coordinates are essential; no dimension-free assertion is made for all flattened color coordinates.

nodes.label: Additive cut responses retain scalar second order
nodes.statement: For finite diagonal common-axis excluded Hamiltonians satisfying the explicit cut parity H(−a)=P H(a)P and polynomial time/input jet bounds, the cut difference has a first Gaussian-field response and a scalar second response. Replacements with small generator errors require, separately, smooth uniformity of their exponential families and lower responses.
nodes.boundary: The extensive uncut Hamiltonian need not have an operator limit. Smallness of a generator on a core alone is not the needed exponential or domain statement.

nodes.label: Exact rooted realization of the scalar coefficient sum
nodes.statement: Fix the same minimizer, 0<T<1 and sufficiently large finite N so the scalar normalizers exist. Set g₀=S and recursively Z_{j+1}=G(g_j), using the same Euler Y_j, c_j and g_j=c_j a(t_{j−1},Y_{j−1})Z_j. Predictability, centering and normalization make g₀,…,g_N orthonormal, hence the Z_j have exactly the independent standard Gaussian law used in F_N. For A_j=E[F_Ng_j] (A₀=0) and B_j=E[F_NZ_j], L*F_N=Σ_{j=0}^N B_{j+1}g_j and E(F_N)=Σ_{j=0}^N A_jB_{j+1}.
nodes.boundary: This realizes both the finite scalar joint law and its shifted energy pairing. It does not assert strong finite-degree convergence for the unsmoothed sign formula. Intermediate transmitted columns need not be bounded.

nodes.label: Finite sign smoothing preserves the rooted value
nodes.statement: For a given minimizer, choose T<1 and then a sufficiently fine finite mesh N. At that fixed T,N, replace F_N=sgn(H_N) by tanh(kH_N). The independent final uniform-rounding coordinate gives P(H_N=0)=0, so this converges in L² as k→∞. For every error>0, finite T,N,k give a centered finite descendant output z with |z|≤1 and E(z)≥P_*−error; local maps are odd and smooth with polynomially bounded derivatives.
nodes.boundary: The order is terminal cutoff, finite scalar mesh, then finite smoothing. The statement has no joint-limit or uniform-in-terminal-time rate and still allows unbounded intermediate columns.

nodes.label: Bounded odd trigonometric angle approximation
nodes.statement: For any fixed finite descendant calculation with odd smooth local maps of polynomial derivative growth, and any η>0, the clipped output m*=clip(z) admits a finite bounded odd angle θ such that ‖sin(2θ)−m*‖<η. All sent columns can be bounded and odd; all pointwise maps can be finite real trigonometric sums with bounded derivatives.
nodes.boundary: The proof first fixes outer Lipschitz constants, then inner errors, using seed truncation, the regularized inverse sine, cutoffs and Fourier approximation. Approximation is in the rooted L² norm, not merely in marginal distribution.

nodes.label: Raw seed reencoding and ancestor exclusion
nodes.statement: A single raw standard Gaussian is measurably recoded into an even finite color and an independent odd Gaussian seed; the induced rooted isometry intertwines L. For a fixed bounded odd smooth formula with bounded first derivatives, excluding current color, all path-ancestor colors and all helpers gives ‖f_col−f‖²≤C(α+p_H), where α is the largest nonhelper color probability and C depends on the fixed uncolored formula, not the number of colors. The output vanishes on helpers.
nodes.boundary: Disjoint mask orthogonality and the Gaussian isometry control the loss. Shared descendant branches are not assumed independent. Uniform derivative bounds refer to the original grouped coordinates.

nodes.label: Conditional bounded synthesis input for a given minimizer
nodes.statement: For every supplied admissible zero-temperature minimizer γ, every ε>0 and η_H>0, the same γ may be used to choose finite T,N,k, a bounded trigonometric formula and finite colors with one positive-probability helper type per propagation depth, total 0<p_H<η_H. The resulting m_col=Σ_c1_{C=c}sin(2θ_c) is centered, bounded by one, zero on helper roots, obeys all current/ancestor/helper exclusions and has E(m_col)≥P_*−ε. All choices are independent of D,n,J.

nodes.label: Closed existence of a near-optimal bounded synthesis input
nodes.statement: For every ε>0 and η_H>0 there exists a zero-temperature minimizer γ and one common finite set of cutoff, scalar-mesh, smoothing, trigonometric and color/helper choices producing a centered m_col with |m_col|≤1, E(m_col)≥P_*−ε and 0<p_H<η_H. Its bounded odd angle/column formulas have the prescribed exclusions and bounded continuous derivatives conditional on labels. Every coefficient, depth, law and function is fixed independently of D,n,J.

Its annotated support edge exposes the conditional argument while discharging the supplied manuscript admissibility and minimizer premises only within this use. nodes.statement: For each fixed finite excluded calculation, even X and odd Y/Z seed functions are approximated by finitely many elementary seed and mixer gates; finite sign averaging isolates the desired disjoint-mask costs. Finite product and group-commutator formulas converge with all required local jets and adjoint jets and polynomial weighted domination in a fixed surrounding calculation.

nodes.label: Orthogonal mask quadratics have small exponentials
nodes.statement: For disjoint-mask real commuting columns d_l,e_l with weighted norms at most C_a√p_l, the centered quadratic Q=Σ_l(q(d_l)q(e_l)−⟨d_l,e_l⟩) is O_sm(ρ), ρ=(Σ_l p_l²)^(1/2). For disjoint receiver I and sender J with excluded seed-only bounded odd transmitted f, refine J into J_l and use the I–J_l–K–J_l commutator paths with the 1/p_K factor. On the recursively compressed space pinning X=1 at every helper descendant, finitely many such propagations converge simultaneously as max_l p_l→0. Root maps and adjoints converge conditionally modulo harmless root-seed phases; off-helper insertions converge.

Individual approximating commutator factors need not preserve that subspace. Lower first responses and scalar second responses must be retained; covariance between channels cannot be discarded.

Its high directions ℓ_r,w_r are centered unit vectors, asymptotically orthogonal, and escape every fixed number sector. Combining the two actual huge costs before approximation gives the finite Weyl displacement (t/r)(v′−v)=−2t w_r+o(1), modulo a spin-independent phase, and updates each special center by D↦D−t(v+v′).

A one-child replacement estimate of order 1/D and Efron–Stein give uniform first child occupation. For centered equivariant outputs, the root-shift energy therefore equals the scaled edge limit.
